source_text: Περὶ τοῦ μὴ τοῖς ὄχλοις ἐπιτρέπειν τὰς ἐκλογὰς ποιεῖσθαι τῶν μελλόντων καθίστασθαι εἰς ἱερατεῖον. Ἐ ρ μ η ν ε ί α. Ἐμποδίζει ὁ παρών Κανών, τὸ νά κάμνουσιν οἱ ὄχλοι καὶ τὰ ἄτακτα πλήθη τῶν πόλεων τάς ψήφους καὶ τάς ἐκλογὰς ἐκείνων ὅπου μέλλουν να χειροτονηθουν Ἱερεῖς (ἢ καὶ Ἀρχιερεῖς), α. ὅτι κατὰ προηγούμενον μὲν λόγον οἱ τοιοῦτοι πρέπει νά ψηφίζωνται ἀπὸ τοὺς Ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ συνιερεῖς, ἑπομένως δὲ νά συμψηφίζωνται καὶ ἀπὸ τὸν λαόν• καὶ β΄. ὅτι ἴσως οἱ φρονιμώτεροι καὶ εὐλαβέστεροι λαϊκοὶ πρέπει νά συμψηφίζουν μὲ τοὺς Ἐπισκόπους καὶ Ἱερεῖς, τὸν μέλλοντα χειροτονηθῆναι εἰς αὐτοὺς Ἱερέα(ἢ καὶ Ἀρχιερέα), ἀλλ’ ὄχι καὶ ὁ χύδην καὶ ἄτακτος ὄχλος, διὰ τάς ἔριδας καὶ μάχας ὅπου ἠμποροῦν νά γεννηθοῦν εἰς τάς ψηφοφορίας αὐτῶν, ἄλλων μὲν ἄλλον ψηφιζομένων, καὶ ἄλλων ἄλλον. Ὅρᾳ καὶ τὴν ὑποσημείωσιν τοῦ ε΄. τῆς παρούσης, καὶ τὸν λ΄. καὶ ξα΄. Ἀποστολικόν.
thought_title: Elections to the priesthood must not be left to the crowds
orientation: The council is giving its own rule, with an attached explanation, that the disorderly crowds of the cities must not make the elections of those about to be ordained priests or high priests.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning not permitting the crowds to make the elections of those about to be appointed to the priesthood. Explanation. The present Canon hinders the crowds and the disorderly multitudes of the cities from making the votes and the elections of those who are about to be ordained Priests (or also High Priests), first, because according to the prior reason such men must be voted for by the High Priests and fellow priests, and then also be voted together with by the people; and second, because perhaps the wiser and more pious laymen must vote together with the Bishops and Priests for the one about to be ordained as Priest for them (or also High Priest), but not also the vulgar and disorderly crowd, because of the quarrels and fights that can be born in their votings, some voting for one man, and others for another. See also the note on the fifth of the present, and the thirtieth and sixty-first Apostolic.

choices.why: The noun denotes the priestly office or order into which candidates are appointed; 'priesthood' keeps the institutional sense.
The source uses the term for bishops in the ecclesiastical hierarchy; capitalizing preserves the title's weight.
The adjective means unruly or undisciplined, and the noun means crowds or masses; the pairing stresses the mob character the canon rejects.
The verb specifically means ordination by laying on of hands, not mere appointment.
The compound verb means to cast a vote along with others, preserving the cooperative sense of the laity's role.
The adverb means 'in a heap' or 'promiscuously,' describing the undifferentiated common crowd; 'vulgar' captures the pejorative sense.

pass_b_english: Concerning not permitting the crowds to hold elections for those who are to be appointed to the priesthood. This canon forbids the crowds and the disorderly multitudes of the cities from casting votes and holding elections for those who are about to be ordained as priests (or even as bishops). First, because by the primary argument such men must be voted on by the High Priests and their fellow priests, and subsequently the people should join in the vote as well. Second, because perhaps the wiser and more devout laity ought to vote together with the bishops and priests for the man who is to be ordained as their priest (or even as bishop), but not the vulgar and disorderly mob, on account of the quarrels and fights that can arise in their voting, when some vote for one man and others for another. See also the note on canon 5 of this council, and Apostolic Canons 30 and 61.

problems.fix: First, because by the primary argument such men must be voted on...
problems.ruling: λόγον means reason/argument, not rule (κανών); mistranslates source.

problems.ruling: Ἀρχιερεῖς in Christian context means bishops; 'High Priests' misleads readers into thinking of Jewish hierarchy.
